sections.text:
* Correspondence: chenbing@gedi.com.cn
Abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet, cloud computing, big data, artificial
intelligence, and other information technologies, data centers have become a crucial part of
modern society’s infrastructure, which puts forward very high requirements for the safety
and reliability of power supply. Most of the servers, networks, and other equipment in data
centers are DC-driven loads, which can significantly enhance resource utilization efficiency
by efficiently accessing the DC power supply through voltage source converter-based
high-voltage direct current transmission and distribution technology. For this reason, this
paper first proposes a multi-level network topology design method for AC/DC distribution
systems in the context of data centers. Based on the analysis of the adaptability of AC/DC
distribution systems in data center access, the design and analysis of its multi-level network
topology is carried out at the physical level for the construction of hybrid AC/DC distri-
bution systems in data center. On this basis, a time series multi-scenario planning model
of AC/DC distribution system with distributed generation in data center is established,
the configuration strategy of AC/DC distribution system is investigated, and a time series
multi-scenario optimization planning method for hybrid AC/DC distribution systems
in data centers is proposed. Finally, the validity of the proposed method is verified by
simulation examples.
Keywords: data center; AC/DC distribution system; network topology; time series multi-
scenario; optimization planning

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.text:
In recent years, data centers have become an important part of the construction of
infrastructure in modern society [1,2]. Data centers, as gathering places for information
and computing resources, have huge demands and high-reliability requirements for power
supply [3]. Most of the servers, networks, and other equipment in the data center are
DC-driven loads. Efficient access to DC power supply through voltage source converter-
based distribution technology can greatly enhance energy efficiency and reduce carbon
emissions [4,5]. The use of the voltage source converter and its core equipment to build a
new DC energy power supply system can promote multi-energy synergies, and give play
to the independent control of active and reactive power, ensuring that the data center load
supply is more reliable and secure.
As one of the important directions of the ‘new infrastructure’, the energy saving
and consumption reduction of data centers has always been the focus of research in the
Electronics 2025, 14, 264 https://doi.org/10.3390/electronics14020264
Electronics 2025, 14, 264 2 of 21
field [6]. The construction of AC/DC distribution systems in the context of data centers is
a critical link to ensure the power supply of data centers. The introduction of DC power
supply form to construct the AC/DC power distribution system in data center design can
effectively guarantee the efficient and reliable operation of a system which has a high data
concentration and needs to be uninterruptedly powered for a long time. A DC power
supply system is better than traditional AC power supply in terms of reliability and stability
and can be promoted and applied in data center scenarios. Famous enterprises in the data
industry at home and abroad have also carried out the practice of DC power distribution in
data centers. At present, there have been studies at home and abroad that have introduced
various topologies of DC power distribution systems. The literature [7] lists the common DC
distribution network topologies which can be categorized as chain topology, ring topology,
and double-ended topology. The chain structure is simple and convenient to implement, but
a short circuit fault in any line will affect the intermediate converter station, and the impact
of a short circuit fault in a DC line on each converter station is relatively small. The reliability
of power supply in the ring system is high, but it is not convenient for the expansion of the
system, and when a fault occurs in any converter station, the fault current affects all parts
of the system. Literature [8,9] proposes a dual-supply DC distribution network structure
without DC circuit breakers by replacing the DC circuit breakers with load switches and the
half-bridge MMC converters with full-bridge MMC converters, based on the dual-supply
topology of the ±10 kV flexible DC distribution network demonstration project in Tongli,
Suzhou, China. The literature [10] focuses on the dynamic reconfiguration of an AC/DC
distribution system and combines network reconfiguration with energy management.
Thereby, a two-stage energy management scheme (EMS) of AC/DC hybrid intelligent
distribution systems (DSs) was proposed to solve the energy management problem of
AC/DC hybrid systems considering network reconfiguration. The literature [11] proposes
a hybrid AC/DC distribution network (HADDN) reactive voltage control method based on
a two-stage robust optimization model. This method can effectively coordinate traditional
reactive voltage equipment and AC/DC converter stations, seek robust optimal coordinated
control schemes, and effectively deal with the uncertainty of renewable energy. With the
continuous development and expansion of data centers, DC distribution systems will
have broad development prospects and practical significance. The literature [12] presents
results of short circuit to ground simulation in an exemplary DC data center, the challenges
of the proper control and protection system design, and discusses zone selectivity as a
possible solution for fast and exact fault location. In [ 13], a novel low-voltage direct-
current (LVDC) superconducting power distribution system and corresponding controller
designed for data centers is proposed to improve power quality and reduce transmission
losses simultaneously. The literature [14] proposes a new control scheme of power data
centers based on DC power supply and distribution technology. In [ 15], a method for
tuning the fractional exponent of different types of fractional order resonant controllers
for a voltage source converter is proposed, which can be applied in a data center with
a DC power supply. In [ 16], a concept of a data center-integrated energy system (DC-
IES) is introduced, and its generalization, approaches, methods, techniques, and future
perspectives are scrutinized in the utilization of renewable energy, recovery of waste heat,
construction of producer and consumer and diversity of system architecture, as well as
optimization solutions in DC-IES planning and design. The literature [ 17] presents an
overview of the data center power supply system covering the power delivery path from
the grid edge to onboard point-of-load conversion, while the power conversion stages of
the data center power supply system are discussed as AC/DC conversions and DC/DC
conversions. In [ 18], a full DC power supply system, incorporating renewable energy
sources and large-scale energy storage, is constructed and comprehensively evaluated.
Electronics 2025, 14, 264 3 of 21
However, research on the design of AC/DC distribution system network topology for data
center access is still under exploration. How to combine the specific needs of a data center,
such as security, reliability, and a large proportion of DC loads, and carry out the design
and analysis of its multi-level network topology from the physical level, is still the first key
difficulty in the construction of an AC/DC distribution network for data centers.
On the other hand, traditional distribution network planning is to carry out line modi-
fication, load expansion, and network reconfiguration based on the existing power structure
and load forecast during the planning level year. After the infiltration of distributed gener-
ation and data center loads, the differences in their types, grid-connected locations, and
installed capacities will have a great impact on the distribution network by changing the
network node structure and operation mode. To maximize the benefits and reduce the
negative impacts of distributed generation, it is necessary to carry out reasonable planning
for the AC/DC distribution network under the access of distributed generation and data
center loads. In summary, the massive infiltration of DG and the continuous increase of
DC load density in data centers have increased the uncertainties faced in the planning and
operation of AC/DC distribution systems in data centers, and research continues on the
planning methods of AC/DC distribution systems in data centers for different time series
application scenarios.
For this reason, this paper first proposes a multi-level network topology design method
for AC/DC distribution systems for the data center. Based on analyzing the adaptability
of access to the AC/DC distribution system in data centers, the design and analysis of its
multi-level network topology are carried out at the physical level for the construction of
AC/DC distribution systems in data centers. On this basis, a time series multi-scenario
planning model for AC/DC distribution systems with distributed generation in data centers
is established, and a method of time series multi-scenario optimization planning for data
center application scenarios is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method
is verified by simulation examples.

sections.text: Systems in Data Centers

sections.title: 2.1 Adaptability Analysis of AC/DC Distribution System Access in Data Centers
sections.text:
The traditional data center solution is to provide a medium-voltage AC distribution
circuit (typically 10 kV or 20 kV , from various 110 kV stations or bus sections) of sufficient ca-
pacity through the existing AC distribution system [19,20]. When DC supply is introduced,
direct DC can be taken into account from the medium-voltage 10 kV incoming source down
to the low-voltage distribution section close to the end loads. With the introduction of
DC transmission and distribution, access to green energy becomes more straightforward.
Photovoltaics, large-scale energy storage batteries, and future backup hydrogen fuel cells
are all DC output interfaces [21]. From an electrical point of view, the access to the above
systems, in addition to their DC interfaces, offers significant advantages in terms of system
harmonics over traditional AC solutions.
Voltage level selection is the basis of distribution network planning, and the main
factor for DC voltage level selection, which is most critical in AC/DC distribution systems
in data centers, including both internal and external factors.
(1) Internal factor
a. Economic impact
The cost of equipment acquisition is a large investment: the equipment of the DC
distribution system currently contains DC converters, DC transformers, power electronic
transformers, DC circuit-breakers, and so on. This key equipment is now generally higher
Electronics 2025, 14, 264 4 of 21
than the cost of AC power distribution equipment, causing the power system to increase
the one-time investment.
Small footprint: The footprint of the electrical equipment room of a data center using
a DC distribution system is approximately one-third that of an AC distribution system.
Compared to a traditional data center power supply scheme, the footprint is reduced by
50 percent, with a 40-percent saving in the amount of equipment and engineering work.
b. Technical impact
Smooth and reliable. The DC distribution system is connected to the AC grid through
the DC converter, which has a certain fault ride-through capability and fault protection
capability, and can effectively prevent the expansion of the scope of influence of the fault.
Flexible and controllable. The DC interconnection does not require consistency in
phase, frequency and amplitude, so it can realize the interconnection of power sources of
different natures, guarantee load transfer, and make full use of the power supply capacity
of different power sources.
High quality and efficiency. The converter in DC distribution system can flexibly and
dynamically compensate the reactive power of AC bus and user loads, stabilize the AC
voltage of AC bus and user side, and the line loss of the DC power distribution system is
much lower, compared with the conventional AC power distribution system, the loss saving
being about 5–8%. When the convergence radius is more than 5 km, and the convergence
capacity is not less than 10 MW, it is more economical to use the medium-voltage DC
method of convergence. Here, the convergence radius within AC/DC grids, commonly
referred to as the physical distance along the line from a power source point (such as a
distribution transformer or a DC power source point) to the farthest load point it supplies,
ensures that the power grid can quickly restore power supply in case of failures, thereby
reducing the duration and scope of power outages.
(2) External factors
Social development influences the selection of the DC power supply mode and reason-
able voltage level. With the continuous development of socio-economic factors, climbing
economic aggregates create a rapid growth in electricity consumption, which requires the
distribution system to deliver a higher capacity to ensure the power to meet the needs
of national economic development, it is very important to reduce loss and improve the
efficiency of power use. Moreover, DC loads in distribution networks will account for an
increasing proportion in the future, especially in data centers (parks) where DC loads will
gradually dominate, and the establishment of DC distribution networks will reduce power
conversion links and significantly improve power supply efficiency.
2.2. Multi-Level Network Topology Design for AC/DC Distribution Systems in Data Centers
Based on the nature of data center usage and the degree of economic or social loss
or impact caused by data loss or network disruption, data centers are classified into three
tiers: A, B, and C. Tier A is a ’fault-tolerant’ system with the highest level of reliability
and availability; Tier B is a ’redundant’ system with intermediate levels of reliability and
availability; and Tier C meets basic needs with the lowest level of reliability and availability.
According to TIA, or The Uptime Institute, data center rooms can be classified into four
tiers ranging from ‘Tier I’ (systems with no redundant components) to ‘Tier IV’ (systems
with redundant components and capable of uninterrupted maintenance). In terms of power
supply configuration, GB50174 corresponds to the TIA-942 or Uptime standard as shown
in Table 1 below.

sections.title: 4.1 Solution Methodology
sections.text:
Define the Pareto dominance relation: in a minimization multi-objective optimization
problem, for n objective components fi(x), i = 1 . . .n, given any two decision variables
Xa, Xb, Xa is said to dominate Xb, if the following two conditions hold:
(1) fi(Xa) ≤ fi(Xb) holds for ∀i ∈ 1, 2 . . .n.
(2) ∃i ∈ 1, 2 . . .n, such that fi(Xa) < fi(Xb) holds.
Define Pareto rank: in a set of solutions, the Pareto rank of the non-dominated solution
is defined as 1. Removing the non-dominated solution from the set of solutions, the Pareto
rank of the non-dominated solution in the remaining solutions is defined as 2, and so on,
which gives all the Pareto ranks in the set of solutions.
(1) The degree of crowding
In order to make the obtained solution more homogeneous in the objective space, the
degree of crowding between the decision variables is introduced as follows:

(2) Elite retention strategy
Firstly, the parent population Ci and the child population Di are synthesized into the
population Ri, and then a new parent population Ci+1 is generated from the population Ri
according to the following rules:
(1) According to the order of Pareto rank from low to high, the whole layer of the
population is put into the parent population Ci+1 until a certain layer of individuals in that
layer cannot all be put into the parent population Ci+1;

(2) Individuals in the layer are arranged from largest to smallest according to the
degree of crowding and are placed into the parent populationCi+1 in order until the parent
population Ci+1 is filled.

sections.title: 4.2 Planning Process
sections.text:
Firstly, the initial population of size N is randomly generated, and the first generation
of offspring population is obtained through the three basic operations of selection, crossover,
and mutation of the genetic algorithm; secondly, the parent and offspring populations are
combined from the second generation onwards to carry out the fast non-dominated order-
ing, and at the same time, the crowding degree of each individual in the non-dominated
layer is computed, and the suitable individuals are selected according to non-dominated
relationship and crowding degree of individuals to form the new offspring population;
finally, a new offspring population is generated through the basic operation of a genetic
algorithm. This continues until the conditions for the end of the procedure are met. The
planning and solving process is shown is Figure 6 and as follows:

5.1 Example of Topology Evolution of AC/DC Distribution Systems in Data Centers
sections.text:
(1) Single-stage planning
Using a 13-node system, in order to visually compare the impact of new energy
and data center DC loads on the overall distribution network morphology and structure
after penetration into the distribution network, this paper designs two future distribution
network operation scenario time sections for comparative analysis.
Scenario 1: Contains distributed PV and WT, DC loads and AC loads in a data center.
Scenario 2: Contains distributed PV and WT, and contains only AC loads (the DC
loads of Scenario 1 are superimposed on the AC loads).
Electronics 2025, 14, 264 13 of 21
According to the data, the discount rate in the calculation example is taken as 7.5%, the
unit capacity of VSC converter is $170/kVA, the line investment is $28,000 per kilometer,
the conversion efficiency of the converter is 95%, the planning life is 15 years, and the cost of
conventional power output is $100/MWh. The morphological structure of the distribution
network obtained by the two-layer optimization model is shown in Figure 7 below (the
black line indicates AC and the red line indicates DC):

In Scenario 2, the DC load penetration of the data center is 0%, while the DC distrib-
uted generation distribution points are relatively few, and the AC component occupies a 
major part of the distribution network topology. At this time, the DC bus transformation 
tends to select DC distributed generation an d network buses, such as bus 4 and bus 11, 
because it can save the investment cost of the converter and reduce the converter loss. 
In Scenario 1, due to the presence of a la rge number of DC loads in the data center, 
the DC component occupies a major part of the distribution network topology. In this 
case, the buses with DC loads or new energy units have a be tter chance of being selected 
as DC buses, such as bus 3, bus 11, and bus 12, and the buses with AC loads or new energy 
units have a better chance of being selected as AC buses, such as bus 2 and bus 13, because 
it can save the investment cost of the converter and reduce the loss of the converter; there 
are AC and DC components in the buses, and the selection of the bus type depends on the 
ratio of AC and DC components in the buses, the topology of the distribution network, 
and so on. 
From the distribution network form optimization results of Scenario 1 and Scenario 
2 above, it can be seen that with the penetration of new energy and DC loads in the data 
center into the traditional distribution network, in order to keep the operation and invest-
ment costs of the distribution network at a minimum during the planning cycle, on the 
one hand, DC components will be introduced into the distribution network; on the other 
hand, the proportion of the introduced DC components is related to the proportion of new 
energy and DC loads in the data center, with  a higher proportion of which the introduc-
tion of DC component is greater.

The optimal morphology of the distribution network varies with the scenarios of the
